items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Final explicit decisions F,P,F contain two correct indications versus F,P,P. Unsolicited historical explanation has serious errors; the rubric scores the indications.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: The final phrase Związanie Hanzańskie recognisably identifies the Hanseatic association. Borderline linguistic acceptance of a malformed name; most of the response is irrelevant town-plan discussion.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Says the plan follows Lubeck law and identifies the absent market square and broad market street in Elblag. These satisfy the core requirement despite spurious extra claims about cities appearing in the plan.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Crecy rather than the Hundred Years War and invents a return of France to Poland.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Links the claim to Charles IVs death and Philip IVs grandson through Isabella. Borderline award consistent with v3: a correct genealogical explanation is accompanied by a false opening about a 1327 abdication.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Does not identify French lilies alongside English lions on Edwards standard; no required graphical explanation.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Proposed patriotism similarity is unsupported; the difference misreads the first source and invents rule during Casimir the Great. No correct shared assessment or change-versus-limited-horizons contrast.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Both Gothic and Renaissance styles are named correctly, which explicitly earns one point. The stated black/silver features are not valid architectural features, so no second point.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Invents a bishop being lifted by benches and gives no valid argument about the Bible outweighing Catholic symbols or rejection of church hierarchy.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Kazimierz Jagiellonczyk instead of Zygmunt III Waza; the surrounding genealogy is also wrong.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Discusses an invented genealogy and gives no Baltic or Livonian territorial cause of the wars.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Explicit indications F,F,P match two of the keyed P,F,P decisions. Unsolicited explanations contain errors and a contradictory sentence, so this is not evidence of sound reasoning.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Explicitly describes veto as a weapon in political struggle leading to breakdown of parliament, a rubric-accepted explanation. Repetition and garbled additional phrasing do not change that central mechanism.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Correct no, but justification invents Enlightenment references in the source and never distinguishes three legislative estates from the separation of powers.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Identifies Ostroleka but selects map A rather than the required B.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Repeats the source narrative instead of choosing C or stating the relation to Olszynka Grochowska.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Janusz Kowalski instead of Ignacy Lukasiewicz.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Talks about the oil industry and dates but never names the Austrian partition or Galicia.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Gives Romanticism and Gothic references rather than realism and a valid realist feature.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: States agreement and relates both sources to class conflict, proletarian revolution and replacing the social order. Repetitive, but the required comparison is present.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Ladosz and Kraszewski as authors; a separate false claim identifying Marx with John Paul II is not a correct author identification.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Says yes and mentions taxation, but invents a map/documents scene and does not supply a valid visual exploitation contrast between British officials and emaciated Indians.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Misidentifies the aid as Lafayettes personal money/army and explicitly says the USA could not provide funds. No correct US-to-France aid interpretation.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Decisions P,P,P match only one of F,P,F; at least two correct indications are required for a point.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Copies unrelated Versailles/Rapallo discussion without distinguishing the legal Saar plebiscite from illegal Rhineland remilitarisation.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Chooses A,C: recipient wrong, Sikorski as signatory correct. One of two required selections earns one point.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Incorrectly places both alliances on the same side of the Iron Curtain and misidentifies NATO.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Misidentifies the two campaigns as anti-communist and imports Hungary 1956; fails to distinguish the 1968 antisemitic and anti-Church campaigns.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Brezhnev correctly but does not explain the strikes, Solidarity or crisis of communist power required with that identification.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: Names Brezhnev rather than Jaruzelski and gives no correct explanation of martial law against Solidarity.

items.grader: Codex rubric review; provisional, not official
items.grade_reason: A=0/12: invented Stefan Zbigniew I, Sobieski and Poniatowski with the 1791 constitution do not support an 11th-12th-century argument. B=0/3: 271 whitespace-delimited words, below 300, with repetition and logical disorder.

notes: Provisional Codex rubric review, not official grading or a passing claim.
Same public development paper inspected during search-policy development; later held-out evaluation required.
Only retrieval policy changed; same 89-article corpus, answering prompt, model weights and budget.
One local run per configuration; timing is descriptive, not a repeated speed benchmark.
Keys and rubrics kept outside solver and retrieval.
All 35 successful evidence traces match the pre-run audit; the two failed rows use labelled offline reconstruction.

disputed_positive_awards.reason: Correct genealogical explanation with false opening circumstance/date

grading_sensitivity.note: Selected judgement sensitivity only; not a confidence interval or exhaustive uncertainty estimate. Other awarded answers include extraneous errors. Previous v3 also had two disputed awards.
